title: Strip harness <system-reminder> blocks from Claude Code user turns at ingest, keeping any person text after the tag; add fixture
notes: Found 2026-11-23 installing a fresh instance on a second macOS machine (Darwin 27.2, uv 0.11, pnpm 11) following syntopica AGENTS.md.

On a first ingest of claude-code conversations, 'atrium search' returned a user-role record whose text begins with '<system-reminder>' (harness-injected context, not the person's words). It pollutes retrieval and may carry account context into the index.

2026-11-24 audit: not done. No stripping exists: atrium/ingest/machine_prompt_prefixes.py deliberately leaves <system-reminder> out of the reject list (194 of 236 messages carry person text after the tag), so such records are admitted whole; tests/test_admission_breakdown.py only asserts the counting of one. Next step: strip the <system-reminder>...</system-reminder> spans from user text at ingest (reject if nothing remains), then add a fixture.
done_when: Ingest drops or strips system-reminder content from user turns; a fixture covers it
result: Strip harness <system-reminder> blocks from Claude Code user turns at ingest, keeping any person text after the tag; add fixture
evidence: strip_system_reminders removes closed system-reminder blocks from user turns in to_records before admission; a reminder-only turn yields no record. tests/test_system_reminder_stripping.py failed first (4 of 6) and passes; 'uv run pytest tests/test_system_reminder_stripping.py tests/test_ingest.py -q' 19 passed; ruff and mypy clean. Records already indexed keep their text until re-ingest.
